q: When judging an online source, which criterion asks how recently the information was published or updated?
o: Currency
Authority
Accuracy
Relevance
x: Currency is about the date: whether the information is up to date. Authority asks who wrote it and whether they are qualified.

q: A student searches for `cricket` and then for `cricket AND Lahore`. Compared with the first search, the second search usually returns:
o: more results, because two words are searched
the same results in a different order
only pages that contain neither word
fewer results, because each page must contain both words
x: AND narrows a search: a page must contain cricket and also Lahore, so some cricket pages drop out. It is OR that widens a search.

q: A message forwarded on social media claims that the exam board has cancelled this year's papers. What is the best first step before believing or sharing it?
o: Share it at once, since many people have already forwarded it
Check the exam board's official website or trusted news sources for the same news
Believe it if the message shows the board's logo
Forward it to friends and ask them to check it
x: Checking the original, official source shows whether the claim is real. Many forwards or a copied logo prove nothing, because fake messages spread and logos are easy to copy.

q: A student wants web pages about smog that do not mention Delhi at all. Using Boolean operators, which search should she type?
o: `smog AND Delhi`
`smog OR Delhi`
`smog NOT Delhi`
`"smog Delhi"`
x: NOT removes every page that contains the word after it, so only smog pages without Delhi remain. AND would keep only pages that mention both words, OR would add Delhi pages, and quotation marks search for the exact phrase “smog Delhi”.

q: Which question does the Purpose criterion ask when evaluating an online source?
o: When was it published or last updated?
Who wrote it, and are they qualified?
Is it supported by evidence that can be checked?
Why was it written: to inform, or to sell or persuade?
x: Purpose asks why the source exists, since a page written to sell or persuade may be one-sided. The date question is currency, the writer question is authority and the evidence question is accuracy.

q: A library database has 40 articles that contain the word robot, 25 that contain the word sensor, and 10 that contain both. How many articles does the search `robot OR sensor` return?
x: OR returns articles with either word, but the 10 with both must be counted once: 40 + 25 − 10 = 55. 65 counts those 10 twice, and 10 is the answer for `robot AND sensor`.

q: In design thinking, what happens in the Define stage?
o: Many possible solutions are brainstormed
The users' main problem is stated clearly as a problem statement
A simple, early model of the solution is built
Users try the solution and give feedback
x: After Empathize, the Define stage turns what was learnt about users into a clear statement of their problem. Brainstorming solutions is Ideate, building a model is Prototype and user feedback is Test.

q: A team writes down as many ideas as possible for an app that helps students share notes, without judging any idea yet. Which design thinking stage is this?
o: Define
Prototype
Ideate
Test
x: Generating many possible solutions freely is the Ideate stage. Prototype comes next, when a chosen idea is turned into a simple model.

q: In a SWOT analysis for a new food-delivery startup, which of these is a Strength?
o: Online ordering is growing fast in the city
A large company may start a cheaper service
Its founders have strong app-development skills
It has little money for advertising
x: Strengths and weaknesses are internal to the business; the founders' skills are an internal advantage. Growing online ordering is an external Opportunity, a rival is a Threat and a small budget is a Weakness.

q: In a business plan, what is the executive summary?
o: A short overview of the whole plan, placed at its start
A detailed list of every expense
The CVs of all the employees
A list of references at the end
x: The executive summary briefly states the idea, market, team and finances so a reader such as an investor gets the whole picture first. Detailed costs belong in the financial section.

q: Which part of a business plan estimates the expected sales, costs and profit for the next few years?
o: Market analysis
Financial projections
Executive summary
Product description
x: Financial projections forecast revenue, costs and profit. Market analysis studies the customers and competitors that those forecasts are based on.

q: An online shop sells 150 shirts a month at Rs 800 each. Each shirt costs Rs 500 to make, and the shop's fixed costs are Rs 30,000 a month. What is its monthly profit?
x: Each shirt earns 800 − 500 = Rs 300 over its cost, so 150 × 300 = Rs 45,000; minus fixed costs of Rs 30,000 leaves Rs 15,000 profit. Rs 45,000 forgets the fixed costs, and Rs 120,000 is the sales revenue.
